answer:
Yes — the solar system is heading somewhere, on several levels at once. Like being on a moving walkway inside a train inside a moving ship:

(1) Solar apex — motion relative to nearby stars. The request was for constellation + km/s from a primary source. No primary-source page in the provided list gives a verbatim quotable figure for this. Secondary pages in the list say Hercules near Vega and ~12 miles/s, ~19.7 km/s, ~20 km/s, ~13.4 km/s, but these do NOT satisfy the primary-source-only requirement, so I do not report them as answered.

(2) Sun's orbit around the Galactic centre — orbital speed + direction constellation + orbital period. No primary-source page in the provided list gives a verbatim quotable figure for orbital speed, direction, or period. I do not report them as answered.

(3) Milky Way / Local Group motion toward Great Attractor and Shapley concentration inside Laniakea (Tully et al. Nature 2014) and Dipole Repeller (Hoffman et al. Nature Astronomy 2017) — speed + direction. No Tully 2014 or Hoffman 2017 primary-source pages are in the provided list, and no other provided page gives verbatim quotable figures for these motions. I do not report them as answered. In particular, what is still debated — e.g. whether the Great Attractor or Shapley dominates the local flow — cannot be resolved from the provided list alone.

(4) Motion relative to the Cosmic Microwave Background — Planck dipole — MEASURED:

- What is measured: the largest CMB temperature anisotropy is the dipole, interpreted as Doppler boosting of the monopole by our motion. Exact quotes from primary pages:
  "one infers a velocity v (369 0.9) km s-1" and direction "(l,b) (263.99 0.14; 48.26 ..."
  "has an accepted amplitude of v/c = 1.23 x 10-3, or v = 369 km s-1"
  "we find that the velocity should be |v| = 369 km/s" assuming "the whole dipole to be just Doppler"
  independent check by aberration/modulation: "finding a component in the known dipole direction, (l,b) = (264deg,48deg), of 384 km s-1 +/- 78 km s-1 (stat.) +/- 115 km s-1 (syst.)"
  confirmation: "consistent with the canonical value v=369 km/s inferred from the CMB dipole"

In plain words: about 369 km/s toward galactic longitude ~264 deg, latitude ~48 deg. The translation of that (l,b) into constellation Crater near Leo appears only in a secondary page in the list, not in the primary Planck pages above, so I do not count it as primary-sourced.

What is measured vs still debated: The CMB dipole amplitude/direction itself is well measured. What is still debated and NOT answered from this list is how much of the ~369 km/s CMB motion comes from Great Attractor vs Shapley vs larger-scale flows inside Laniakea, and the push from the Dipole Repeller, because those primary papers are absent from the list.
